topic: Functionality and behavior of llama.cpp's HTTP server file-upload button
problem_or_goal: Understanding how the file-upload button processes input and affects prompt interpretation in llama.cpp's HTTP server
context: An archived Reddit user shared observations about using the file-upload button with llama 3.2 3B Q4_K_S model, noting inconsistent handling of file contents and prompt queries.
motivation: Clarifying the file-upload button's behavior is important for users aiming to query file contents reliably and reproducibly with llama.cpp's HTTP server.
desired_response: Insights or explanations on how the file-upload button integrates file data with prompts, and suggestions for achieving consistent query results.
speaker_relationship_to_source: reader of archived source; no claim of personally running reported tests

facts.text: The file-upload button may concatenate the uploaded file and the direct prompt as a single prompt input.
facts.evidence_quote: Does it simply concatenate the file and my direct prompt, treating the concatenation as the prompt?
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The user observed that no model would yield reliable results if the above concatenation assumption is true.
facts.evidence_quote: but incase my above suspicion is true, that does not matter as no model would yield reliable results.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: In 15 experiments, sometimes the model correctly answered questions about the file's contents.
facts.evidence_quote: In my 15 experiments, sometimes the question about the file's contents is correctly answered.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: Other times, the model interprets the file contents instead of the user's query.
facts.evidence_quote: But sometimes it interprets the contents of the file instead of my query.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The user desires reproducible results when reopening conversations with the same prompts.
facts.evidence_quote: I would like the result to be reproducable, ie when I open a new conversation, giving it the same prompts, I would like to get the same answers
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement
